scripts.name: Node Health
scripts.description:
node-health — is this machine actually fit to take work?

Answers the question a fleet operator asks before dispatching anything: disk, memory, load, and whether a container runtime is up. Runs anywhere, needs no permissions, and touches the network never — which is why it declares `egress=none` rather than leaving it unsaid.

It reports UNKNOWN rather than guessing. A health check that prints a confident number it could not measure is worse than one that says it could not measure it.

scripts.name: Provider payable benchmark — score the engine against Robyn's filed report
scripts.description:
payable-benchmark — score pathways:provider-payable against one of Robyn's filed Case Provider Reports and keep the score, so "are we getting better" is a number with a history.

Two metrics, scored apart because they fail for different reasons: COVERAGE (cases the engine computed / cases she resolved) moves when a data source lands; FIDELITY (rows matching to the cent / rows both computed) moves when the maths reads the right field. Fidelity is split again by whether FreeAgent held a real rate or 70% was assumed.

Refuses to score nothing: if either input parses to zero rows it exits 2 and writes no record.

No network. The fixture is PHI (patient names, DOB) and must already be on the machine; this script never fetches it. Arguments arrive as env vars when run as a Hive script (FIXTURE, ENGINE, RECORD, LABEL, EXCLUDE) and as flags when run by hand.

scripts.name: Photo Resize
scripts.description:
photo-resize — batch-resize a folder of images, without uploading them anywhere.

Reads every JPEG and PNG in the source directory, writes a resized copy to the target, and never touches the network — which is the point. The photos stay on the machine that already has them, which is the whole reason to run this on your own node rather than pasting a folder into somebody's website.

The paths are ARGUMENTS, not baked in. A script that shipped its author's Desktop path would write to a stranger's Desktop.

scripts.name: Provider Capacity
scripts.description:
provider-capacity — decide whether to BUY another metered AI licence or to spend the one you already hold, from two meters you already have: `iris usage --json` (what was consumed, priced at list) and `models:go-usage --json` (how full each licence's windows are).

It answers three questions that are usually collapsed into one and then answered wrongly: 1. LEVERAGE — what would this month's traffic cost at list rates vs what the subscriptions cost? 2. CAPACITY — is the constraint real capacity, or serial routing leaving a spare licence idle? 3. DEMAND — how much of the bill is context re-sent on every turn rather than work done?

Refuses to score nothing: zero calls, or zero readable licences, exits 2 and writes no record. No network. Both inputs are produced by other commands and passed in as files or stdin.

scripts.name: turo-fleet-scraper
scripts.description:
Collect a Turo host's own fleet — listings, per-vehicle photographs, and the aggregate performance record — and print it as JSON on stdout.

Built for CatoDrive, who asked us to use their own Turo images and vehicle information rather than stock photography. Runs against a profile the account owner controls.

mode=stats (~25s) the aggregate: trips, rating, years hosting, review count mode=fleet (~20m) every listing, its trim, and its full photo set

WHY A REAL BROWSER, not fetch(): Turo removed external API access in 2023 and the profile sits behind Cloudflare. A plain request gets HTTP 403 and zero data; headless Chromium gets the interstitial. A headed browser clears the check on its own in about five seconds. This declares requires=browser for that reason — there is no API to call instead.

THREE THINGS THAT LOOK FINE AND ARE NOT, each learned by shipping the wrong version: 1. Photos on a listing page include a "similar cars" rail belonging to OTHER hosts. Scoping to document.images gave 12 photos per car of which 9 were strangers' vehicles — it read as a clean run (1,080 photos) until the tally showed only 569 unique. 2. Turo's CDN serves ONLY the exact size variant the page requested. The bare photo id 404s and so does any size you invent, so the full URL has to be kept verbatim. 3. The gallery shows 3 photos inline; the rest are behind "View N photos".

Reviews are deliberately NOT collected. They are written by named renters for a different platform, and the same feed carries automated "the host canceled this trip" notices — so an import either republishes other people's words without consent or hand-picks the flattering ones. The aggregate below is the host's own record and is verifiable from the profile link.

#!/bin/bash
# iris: arg=seconds default=20
# iris: timeout=120
# A harmless demo for the Hive console: prints, waits, prints again.
echo "console demo starting on $(hostname)"
sleep "${SECONDS_ARG:-${SECONDS:-20}}"
echo "console demo done"
